audit.why: 52.9% over 1603 games. Two level-1 bullies where you hold the point-and-click advantage and he holds the health bar — the page frames it as a close lane you must bank early, which matches.
Spikes sit right: your level 1, your level 3 kill window, your first item, and the two-item stage where his frame outlasts yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings tell you to block 'his empowered Q dash-strike'. That merges two different abilities into one that does not exist.
audit.why: Cull the Meek (Q) is 'swings his blade, dealing moderate physical damage to all targets around him, and heals for a small portion of the damage dealt' — a point-blank AoE swing with no dash in it. The dash is Slice and Dice (E), a separate ability on a separate cooldown that recasts to dash back. Merging them means the player watches the wrong cooldown and braces at the wrong moment: he thinks one button both closes the gap and delivers the big hit, so he holds a 22-second Aegis Assault for a combined thing that arrives in two parts. Worse, the fusion hides the interaction that decides extended trades — Cull the Meek heals Renekton every single cast, on a flat 7s.
audit.corrected: Cull the Meek and Slice and Dice separated, with the heal on Q stated and the dash and recast on E.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly says to fight 'whenever his fury combo is on cooldown' without a single number.
audit.why: The two that matter are both 16s at rank 1: Ruthless Predator at 16/14/12/10/8s and Slice and Dice at 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. Both are longer than your Shield Vault, so either one spent is a window bigger than your own cooldown. Cull the Meek is a flat 7s, so that one is never worth waiting for. Slice and Dice also recasts to dash back through the target, so once he uses the first half he is committed to the return trip.
audit.corrected: Both 16s numbers and the Slice and Dice recast written into mid and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal, on a page whose entire late-game thesis is that he out-grinds you in a drawn-out fight.
audit.why: Cull the Meek heals him on every cast, more so above 50 Fury, and that is precisely the mechanic the late text blames without naming. Grievous Wounds is the direct answer and appears nowhere.

edits.before: Both of us are level-1 bullies, but my point-and-click W stun lands cleaner than his skillshot-less fury fight before he has rage built. If he steps into the wave to last-hit, W onto him, Q, and walk out before he can stun me back. At level 3 hold E to block his empowered Q dash-strike — that directional block eats his biggest hit — then come out of the channel with empowered-Q and the stun for a kill. Don't W in while he's full fury and has W up; bait it first.
edits.after: Both of us are level-1 bullies, but my point-and-click Shield Vault lands before he has fury built. If he steps in to last-hit, vault on, spear, and leave before Ruthless Predator answers. Know which button is which: Cull the Meek (Q) is a point-blank swing that HEALS him on a flat 7s, and the dash is Slice and Dice (E) — separate ability, 16s at rank 1, and it recasts to come back through me. Face Aegis Assault at the swing, not at the dash.

At 6, Grand Starfall is more roam than 1v1 nuke, so use the tempo to leap on a sidelane and bank a second lead rather than forcing a coin-flip into his fury W.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 stay mine. Two cooldowns decide when I commit and both are 16s at rank 1 — Ruthless Predator and Slice and Dice — which is longer than my own Shield Vault, so either one spent is a window bigger than mine. Cull the Meek is a flat 7s and heals him, so never wait that one out. Don't stand in Ruthless Predator range at full fury. At 6, Grand Starfall is roam, not nuke: bank a second lead elsewhere.

edits.before: By two items the lane equalizes fast — we both fall off, but he keeps the bigger HP bar and his fury combo grinds through my squishy frame in a drawn-out fight. My damage plateaus; his doesn't suffer as much because he can soak more. So everything has to be banked early: snowball the level 1-3 windows, take plates and roams, and never let a fed-tempo lead slip into a coin-flip 50/50 at items.
edits.after: By two items the lane equalizes fast — we both fall off, but he keeps the bigger bar and Cull the Meek heals him every 7s through any drawn-out fight, which is exactly why Grievous Wounds is the purchase that keeps me in the duel. Dominus adds health on top. Everything has to be banked early: snowball levels 1-3, take plates and roams, and never let a tempo lead slip into a coin-flip at items.

notes: THE ERROR: three strings told the player to block 'his empowered Q dash-strike'. There is no such ability — the page has fused Cull the Meek and Slice and Dice into one. Cull the Meek is a point-blank AoE swing that heals him; Slice and Dice is a separate dash on a separate 16-second cooldown that recasts to dash back through you. The fusion causes two concrete mistakes: the player watches one cooldown when there are two, and he braces a 22-second Aegis Assault for a combined hit that actually arrives in two parts from two directions. It also hid the mechanic that decides the lane — Cull the Meek heals on every cast, on a flat 7s, which is precisely what the late-game text blames for out-grinding you without ever naming it, and Grievous Wounds appeared nowhere on the page. Best new numbers: Ruthless Predator and Slice and Dice are both 16s at rank 1, longer than Shield Vault, so either one spent gives you a window bigger than your own cooldown, while Cull the Meek at 7s is never worth waiting out.
